title: timeline_adaptation.json — how each shipped timeline event becomes (or does not become) a civic event
$comment: OWNER DECISION, wave 3: the 25/50/25 split is expressed HERE and the timeline catalogs are NOT edited. The rework plan's wording was 'drop the most boring 25% outright', which would have deleted ~30 authored real-history entries from data/timeline_*.json and stopped them firing in the existing timeline system too — a destructive side effect of a story-system wave. A separate policy file gets the same behaviour reversibly: an event marked 'none' keeps firing as a timeline event exactly as it does today and is simply never wrapped into a civic event. One further check runs in the test suite and cannot be expressed here: every id below must name an event that actually exists in timeline_global/eu/na.json.

defaultPolicy.$comment: What an event with no entry below gets. 'generic' means the middle 50% need no entry at all, so the file lists only the two deliberate ends of the split.

policy.$comment: 'none' — never becomes a civic event; it stays a timeline event and nothing else changes. This is the non-destructive form of the plan's 'drop'. 'generic' — the adapter wraps it: name from title, description from headlineBrief, a severity-derived check. 'authored' — a hand-written civic event in data/events_*.json takes over, with real resolution checks and all seven prose fields; civicEventId names it.

civicEventId.$comment: Required when policy is 'authored'. Must name an event in the civic event catalogs.

reason.$comment: Why this event sits at this end of the split. Required by content review for 'none': 'the most boring 25%' is a judgement, and a judgement with no stated reason cannot be argued with later.
